docs.title: Tidewatch
docs.text:
Tidewatch watches your folders and runs tasks when files change. It's a single binary with a small config file, and it's built for the inner loop: rebuild on save, re-run tests, regenerate assets.

$ tidewatch run
tidewatch 1.2.0 · loaded tidewatch.ini (2 sections)
[styles]  watching src/styles/**/*.scss
[tests]   watching src/**/*.py, tests/**/*.py
[tests]   src/parser.py changed → pytest -q  ✓ 1.8s

docs.title: Why Tidewatch
docs.text:
• One config, many tasks. Each [watch:<name>] section has its own paths and command.
  • Delayed runs. Saving 40 files at once triggers one run, not 40.
  • CI friendly. tidewatch run --once runs every section one time and exits.

docs.title: Where to next
docs.text:

  • Quickstart: your first watch section in two minutes.

• ignore key in each [watch:<name>] section.
  • --section flag to run a subset of sections.

• First stable release.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Tidewatch 1.x has a single command.

tidewatch run [options]

docs.title: tidewatch run
docs.text:
Start watching and run sections as files change. Runs until interrupted (Ctrl+C).

Option Description --config <path> Config file to load. Default: ./tidewatch.ini. --section <name> Run only the named section. Repeatable. --once Run every section one time and exit. Exit code 1 if any section fails. (1.1.0+) --quiet Only print command output and errors.

docs.title: tidewatch --version
docs.text: Print the version and exit.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Tidewatch reads tidewatch.ini from the current directory. Use --config <path> to load a different file.

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
tidewatch.ini
[defaults]
delay = 0.2

[watch:styles]
paths = src/styles/**/*.scss
command = sass src/styles:dist/css

[watch:tests]
paths = src/**/*.py, tests/**/*.py
ignore = **/__pycache__/**, **/.pytest_cache/**
command = pytest -q
delay = 0.5

docs.title: [defaults] section
docs.text: Key Type Default Description delay seconds (float) 0.2 Wait this long after the last change before running.

docs.title: [watch:<name>] sections
docs.text:
Each section defines one task. The part after watch: is the task name and log prefix.

Key Type Default Description paths comma-separated globs — Required. Files that trigger the section. ignore comma-separated globs empty Files to exclude, even if they match paths. (1.2.0+) command string — Required. Shell command to run. delay seconds (float) [defaults] value Per-section override.

Glob syntax

* matches within one directory, ** matches across directories. Paths are relative to the directory containing tidewatch.ini.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Tidewatch 1.x ships as a single static binary for Linux and macOS.

macOS / Linux (script)HomebrewCargo 
curl -fsSL https://get.tidewatch.dev/install.sh | sh -s -- --version 1.2.0

brew install tidewatch@1

cargo install tidewatch --version "^1"

docs.title: Verify the install
docs.text:
$ tidewatch --version
tidewatch 1.2.0

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Platform Minimum version File events backend Linux kernel 4.9 inotify macOS 11 (Big Sur) FSEvents

Windows

Windows is not supported in 1.x.

Large repositories on Linux

inotify has a per-user watch limit. If Tidewatch logs too many watches, raise it: sudo sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This guide sets up a section that re-runs your tests every time a Python file changes.

docs.title: 1. Create a config
docs.text:
Create tidewatch.ini in your project root:

tidewatch.ini
[watch:tests]
paths = src/**/*.py, tests/**/*.py
ignore = **/__pycache__/**
command = pytest -q

docs.title: 2. Start watching
docs.text:
$ tidewatch run
tidewatch 1.2.0 · loaded tidewatch.ini (1 section)
[tests] watching src/**/*.py, tests/**/*.py

Save any matching file and Tidewatch runs pytest -q, streaming its output with a [tests] prefix.

docs.title: 3. Run once in CI
docs.text:
Add --once to run every section one time and exit with a non-zero code if any fails:

$ tidewatch run --once
[tests] pytest -q  ✓ 2.1s
